text:
lin (eng-runtime): quick brain dump from today's sync: we need a lower-friction way to avoid fragmentation when tenants request many small resident ranges. thinking about a tier-aware slab allocator + handoff protocol.

ashwin (eng-runtime): sounds useful. can you sketch how handoff works at a high level?

lin (eng-runtime): idea: group allocations into ephemeral "slab sessions" for a tenant/model load. allocator can allocate slabs (contiguous chunk) from GPU or host staging pool. callers can join a slab session instead of individual allocations. when model load finishes, caller returns session token, allocator can pack/migrate or mark slab reclaimable.

noah (eng-ml): that fits model loader patterns. we often load many small tensors then free some. if we had session semantics we could avoid interleaving live tensors from different models. what's the API?

lin (eng-runtime): proto:
StartSlabSession(tenant, tier, target_bytes) -> session_id, granted_bytes
AllocateFromSession(session_id, size, alignment) -> alloc_handle
EndSlabSession(session_id, options) -> reclaim_hint

EndSlabSession options could be COALESCE, RELEASE_IMMEDIATELY, CHECKPOINT_AND_KEEP. reclaim_hint is metadata to help compaction.

sara (eng-sre): ops note: sessions should be bounded by time and have a fallback for stuck clients. we need session_ttl and admin force-drain. also telemetry: session_count, avg_session_lifetime, wasted_bytes_by_session.

ashwin (eng-runtime): agree. also consider a passive compaction path: proactively migrate cold ranges to host staging during low-load windows, compact hot slabs on-demand. there should be a cost budget for compaction to avoid hurting latency.

noah (eng-ml): how do we surface cost to users? e.g., background compaction could spike CPU/GPU memory bandwidth and affect inference. need per-tenant compaction_budget_ms or background_priority.

lin (eng-runtime): plan: default compaction disabled on hosted; enabled on Dedicated by opt-in. config knobs: compaction_window (hh:mm), compaction_budget_pct, allow_session_packing. private deployments can disable force-migration.

ops-bot: cluster `staging-b` alert: GPU memory fragmentation high on node g3-12; affected pods: loader-7, loader-9. Recommended action: evict low-priority sessions.

lin (eng-runtime): thanks bot. that alert proves we need per-session priority and revocable flag. suggest session priorities 0..10 and revocable=true|false. collector can evict revocable sessions first.

noah (eng-ml): SDK ergonomics: provide a context manager helper: with slab_session(bytes, tier, priority) as s: tensor_alloc(s, sizes...). That will make it easy for loaders to adopt. docs should show example for PyTorch/XLA style.

ashwin (eng-runtime): migration considerations: we can't flip allocator semantics overnight. rollout steps:
1) implement session API with soft semantics (just advisory) and expose metrics
2) add SDK helpers and update model-loader libs to use sessions in staging
3) implement revocable sessions and compaction path behind flag
4) after 4 weeks of telemetry, enable force packing on Dedicated opt-ins

sara (eng-sre): add canary: run mixed workload with and without sessions and compare p95 tail latency, OOMs, and fragment_metric. script: `./scripts/session-canary --nodes 10 --duration 2h --variant {session,baseline}`

lin (eng-runtime): good. questions: how does this interact with existing ReserveResident/HintResident tokens? we can make sessions composed of many resident tokens under the hood, or allow sessions to be a higher-level primitive that requests a single big reservation to reduce fragmentation.

noah (eng-ml): prefer single big reservation under the hood for loaders. that reduces allocation churn. but require allocator to be able to split/repack during compaction.

ashwin (eng-runtime): implementer note: make slab sessions map to contiguous address ranges at the allocator level to support fast coalesce and GPU DMA ops. maintain a session->allocation map for quick revocation.

lin (eng-runtime): security/tenancy: enforce tenant-scoped sessions and per-tenant max_session_bytes. admin API to list active sessions and force_end(session_id, reason).

ops-bot: audit log: session_start tenant=acme session=ss-000123 user=noah ts=4801234568

noah (eng-ml): will prototype loader changes this week. can we get a lightweight compatibility shim in the SDK so older callers still get small allocations?

lin (eng-runtime): yes, SDK will fallback to per-allocation path if session APIs unavailable. will include metrics to track adoption.

sara (eng-sre): add alerts: high revocation_rate or compaction_write_bw_pct > 20% during peak hours. and dashboard with fragmentation_ratio per-node.

ashwin (eng-runtime): ok owners: lin -> API + allocator impl (ETA 3w), noah -> SDK + loader adoption (ETA 1w), sara -> canary + alerts (ETA 2d). I'll add this to the RFC as an alternative to token-only approach.

lin (eng-runtime): thanks all. ping me here for objections. i'll push a short follow-up doc with diagrams and a minimal state-machine for sessions. :rocket
